source.title: Learning to Combat Noisy Labels via Classification Margins

page_placements.theme: Generalization peaks and stopping rules depend on training conditions

record.tranche_reason: Reports training-time test accuracy and memorization behavior under partially corrupted labels, bearing on the order in which clean and noisy labels are learned.
record.gate_note: The study tests partial, class-conditional label noise. It does not test completely random labels, unstructured inputs, or whether standard networks fit every training label perfectly. Figure-only curves without reported numeric values are recorded as such. Statements about other papers are excluded.
record.test_reason: The study reports its own cross-entropy training trajectories and noisy-label memorization measurements, directly testing V6 under partial label corruption.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately summarizes the authors' cross-entropy phase observation, although memorization already begins during the apex phase. The paper's main conclusion is that MARVEL and MARVEL+ use margin histories to filter or reweight instances, curb noisy-label memorization and improve generalization.
record.recipe_differences: Experiments study partial class-conditional label noise and training-time memorization, rather than fitting wholly random labels or unstructured inputs.
record.method_sensitivity: Dataset and noise condition vary across experiments; the reported training-phase description used for V6 is CIFAR-10 (cat, dog) with 20% symmetric noise.

fits_no_version.finding: Test accuracy initially improves, plateaus around epochs 20–40, and subsequently declines.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Under partial label noise, cross-entropy training can exhibit an early test-accuracy peak followed by deteriorating generalization.

record.problems: The phase curves are shown without exact values in the supplied text; the memorization ratio requires oracle knowledge of which instances are noisy. The reported V6 experiment covers one dataset/noise condition.
record.rows_left_out: Other test-accuracy and memorization-ratio results compare robust-learning methods across noise settings, but do not directly test the timing claim for standard networks learning real versus random labels. Cited findings from prior work were excluded.

untested.parts: Complete random labeling, zero or near-zero training error, chance test performance, and unchanged hyperparameters relative to true-label training.
Time required to fit true versus random labels and convergence time as corruption increases.
Fitting shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels or Gaussian-noise inputs.

The joint claim of perfect training fit and steadily worsening test error across corruption levels from clean to fully random labels. Test-accuracy tables cover partial noise, but do not establish this joint pattern.
Whether explicit regularizers prevent fitting fully random labels and whether removing them impairs true-label generalization.
Fully random-label training and a direct comparison of representations learned from real versus random labels.

record.verdict_notes: This study is not an original source for the listed versions. Deliberately corrupting training labels does not prescribe memorization or its temporal order; the unmodified cross-entropy baseline provides an empirical test of V6. The proposed methods' mitigation performance does not itself challenge V6.

versions.untested_parts: No experiment assigns completely random labels to the whole training set or reports whether standard networks reach zero or near-zero training error with chance test error.
Does not compare training time to fit true versus random labels or measure convergence time as corruption grows.
No shuffled-pixel, permuted-pixel, or Gaussian-noise input experiments.
Studies partial class-conditional noise, but does not report perfect training fit across corruption levels or a smooth test-error trajectory from clean to fully random labels.
Does not test whether weight decay, dropout, or augmentation prevent fitting random labels, or whether removing them harms true-label generalization.

Tests clean and partially noisy labels, not fully random labels; reports the timing of noisy-label memorization but does not directly compare learned representations or establish the claim for all standard networks.

rows.subject: CE-trained network (CIFAR-10 (cat, dog))
rows.operation_detail: Train with cross-entropy on 20% symmetric label noise; report test accuracy over training epochs.
rows.value: Figure only; text describes learning (epoch 1–20), apex (epoch 20–40), and memorization (epoch 40–100), with test accuracy stopping improving in the apex and declining in memorization.
rows.uncertainty: Mean curve and standard deviation band over 10 runs; numeric uncertainty not stated.
rows.note: The authors describe the training phases in the text; the curve's exact values are not reported.
rows.check: Test accuracy alone cannot establish whether clean labels are fitted before noisy labels; it corroborates R2's timing evidence. Appendix A.1 identifies the network as ResNet-18, trained for 100 epochs using SGD with momentum, weight decay and standard augmentation.

source_check.locator_found: Section 2.2, Figure 1a and caption, page 5; Appendix A.1.

rows.subject: CE-trained network (CIFAR-10 (cat, dog))
rows.operation_detail: Train with cross-entropy on 20% symmetric label noise; report memorization ratio over training epochs.
rows.measure: Memorization ratio: fraction of noisy instances fitted to their noisy labels
rows.value: Figure only; text says the network seemingly disregards noisy instances during learning, begins memorizing them in the apex phase, and continues memorizing them during the memorization phase.
rows.uncertainty: Mean curve and standard deviation band over 10 runs; numeric uncertainty not stated.
rows.note: The memorization ratio uses oracle noise information; the paper's text describes the phase pattern but gives no exact values.
rows.check: The phase description is accurate. Specify ResNet-18 and the Appendix A.1 training setup. Noisy-label accuracy initially decreases, reaches its minimum around epoch 20, stays roughly there for about 10 epochs, then increases; learning-rate decay at epoch 75 increases memorization further. Exact curve values are unavailable in the supplied text.

relationships.reason: R2 and Sections 2.2–3.1 report early learning while noisy-label accuracy decreases, followed by increasing noisy-label memorization during the apex and later phases.
relationships.display_finding: Early learning coincided with decreasing noisy-label accuracy, followed by increasing noisy-label memorization in subsequent training phases.
